# Wikipedia

2 endpoints, all GET. Base URL `https://www.socialcrawl.dev`, auth header `x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY`.

**Credit costs:** 2 standard (1 credit) - the exact cost is in each endpoint heading below.

## GET /v1/wikipedia/article - 1 credit (standard)

Returns one Wikipedia article by its title, in any language Wikipedia publishes: the page id (`post.id`), the title (`post.ext.title`), the article's link and the whole article as plain text (`post.content.text`, section headings kept as `== Heading ==` lines). A redirect is followed to the article it points to. `post.ext.wikipedia` adds the language, whether the page is a disambiguation page listing several meanings, the current revision id, when the page last changed and its size in bytes. A title the Wikipedia does not have answers 404 and is not charged.

**Use when** you want to read an article in full, for research, summaries, entity lookups or grounding an AI answer in a source.
**Cost** cache 600 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `title` (optional, string) - The article's title as Wikipedia shows it, for example Python (programming language). Case matters after the first letter. Send title or url. · e.g. `Python (programming language)`
- `url` (optional, string) - The article's link, for example https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin; its language comes from the link. Send title or url.
- `language` (optional, string) - The Wikipedia's language code, for example en (default), de, fr, ja or simple. Each language is its own Wikipedia with its own articles.

**Constraints**

- Provide at least one of `title`, `url`.

**Response** `Post` object at `data`, `{ computed, post }` ([full schema](schemas/Post.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `post.content.text` | Post caption, description, or text content |
| `post.ext.title` | The post title on its own. |
| `post.id` | Platform-specific post ID… |
| `post.url` | Direct URL to the post on the source platform |
| `computed.content_category` | Keyword-classified content category… |
| `computed.engagement_rate` | Computed engagement rate (0..1). |

+5 more (types in the full schema): `computed` {estimated_reach, language, save_rate}; `post.ext` {wikipedia}; `post.flags` {deleted}. Never filled: `post.author.avatar_url`, `post.author.display_name`, `post.author.username`, `post.author.verified`, `post.content.duration_seconds`, `post.content.media_urls`, `post.content.thumbnail_url`, `post.engagement.comments`, `post.engagement.likes`, `post.engagement.saves`, `post.engagement.shares`, `post.engagement.views` (+1 more).

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/wikipedia/article" \
  --data-urlencode "title=Python (programming language)" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/wikipedia/search - 1 credit (standard)

Returns the Wikipedia articles matching search terms in one language, 10 a page by default and up to 50, for up to 100 pages, with Wikipedia's total for the search. Each result is a Post: the page id (`post.id`, read the article with GET /v1/wikipedia/article by its title), the title (`post.ext.title`), the link and the matching passage as plain text (`post.content.text`). `post.ext.wikipedia` adds the article's word count and when it last changed. Pass the returned cursor for the next page.

**Use when** you want to find the articles about a topic, a person or a company before reading the right one in full.
**Cost** cache 120 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Paging** page (native `page`) · 10/page by default, max 50; set with `limit` · depth unknown · N items ≈ ceil(N/10) x 1 credits

**Query params**

- `query` (required) - Search terms, 1 to 300 characters, for example python programming. · e.g. `python programming`
- `language` (optional, string) - The Wikipedia's language code, for example en (default), de, fr, ja or simple. Each language is its own Wikipedia with its own articles.
- `page` (optional, integer, 1-100) - Page number from 1 to 100. Prefer the universal cursor parameter.
- `limit` (optional, integer, 1-50) - Results per page, 1 to 50. Defaults to 10.
- `since` (optional, string) - Rows published from this date: YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC) or ISO 8601. Rows older than it are left off each page. This list is not in date order, so the walk does not stop at the date: keep following `next_cursor`, and each page costs what a page costs even when every row on it is filtered out. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until).
- **Shared controls** `max_pages` (1-50) → [walks](api-overview.md#search-filters-and-multi-page-walks); `max_items` (1-5000) · `max_credits` (1-100000) → [one-call walks](api-overview.md#get-more-in-one-call-max_items-max_credits-max_pages); `until` → [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until)

**Response** `PostList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ computed, post }` ([full schema](schemas/PostList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `post.content.text` | Post caption, description, or text content |
| `post.ext.title` | The post title on its own. |
| `post.id` | Platform-specific post ID… |
| `post.url` | Direct URL to the post on the source platform |
| `computed.content_category` | Keyword-classified content category… |
| `computed.engagement_rate` | Computed engagement rate (0..1). |

+5 more (types in the full schema): `computed` {estimated_reach, language, save_rate}; `post.ext` {wikipedia}; `post.flags` {deleted}. Never filled: `post.author.avatar_url`, `post.author.display_name`, `post.author.username`, `post.author.verified`, `post.content.duration_seconds`, `post.content.media_urls`, `post.content.thumbnail_url`, `post.engagement.comments`, `post.engagement.likes`, `post.engagement.saves`, `post.engagement.shares`, `post.engagement.views` (+1 more). Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`, `data.walk`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/wikipedia/search" \
  --data-urlencode "query=python programming" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```
